title: Conjecture 1.1 (Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan)
statement_text: For every connected graph $G$ of order $n$, we have $$\min\{s^{+}(G),s^{-}(G)\}\geq n-1.$$
context_text: Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured in 2016 that the positive and negative square energies of any connected graph both exceed $n-1$. It has been verified for hyper-energetic graphs, regular graphs, and other families, and the best unconditional lower bound prior to this paper was $\frac{3n}{4}$.
paper_contribution: Verifies the conjecture for all connected graphs with domination number at most 2, and proves the stronger Conjecture 1.2 (implying Conjecture 1.1) for claw-free graphs and for graphs with diameter 2.
paper_title: Refinement of a conjecture on positive square energy of graphs

title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ and size $m$. If $m\geq n+1$, then $$s^{+}(G)\geq n.$$
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. The super-additivity of square energy over vertex partitions suggests an inductive proof, but the bound $n-1$ is not preserved well under such arguments, which motivates asking when the stronger $s^+(G)\ge n$ holds. Trees have $s^+=n-1$, and unicyclic graphs ($m=n$) can have $s^+<n$ (e.g. cycles of length $1\bmod4$), hence the condition $m\ge n+1$. The conjecture holds for regular graphs and graphs with 1-energy at least $2n$, and has been verified for all connected graphs with at most 9 vertices and for all graphs in the Mathematica database with $n\le100$ and $m\ge n+1$. The authors prove it for claw-free graphs (connected with maximum degree at least 3) and for graphs of diameter 2. The analogue for $s^-$ fails.
paper_title: Refinement of a conjecture on positive square energy of graphs

title: Conjecture 9.1
statement_text: If $G$ is a unicyclic graph of order $n$ whose cycle has odd length $k$, then $s^{+}(G)>n>s^{-}(G)$ if $k\equiv 3\pmod 4$, and $s^{+}(G)<n<s^{-}(G)$ if $k\equiv 1\pmod 4$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. A unicyclic graph is a connected graph with exactly one cycle (so $m=n$). The authors compute cycles exactly: $s^+(C_n)=s^-(C_n)=n$ for even $n$; for $n\equiv3\pmod4$, $s^+(C_n)=n-1+\sec(\pi/n)>n$ and $s^-(C_n)=n+1-\sec(\pi/n)<n$; for $n\equiv1\pmod4$ the roles are exchanged. Unicyclic graphs are believed to be among the hardest cases of the Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture, and this computation together with computer search (no counterexample on at most 9 vertices) leads to the conjecture.

title: Conjecture 9.2
statement_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$. $s^{+}(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a tree. $s^{-}(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a tree or a complete graph.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. The conjecture characterizes the equality cases $s^+(G)=n-1$ and $s^-(G)=n-1$ in the Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture. For a tree, which is bipartite, $s^+=s^-=m=n-1$; for the complete graph $K_n$, the eigenvalues are $n-1$ and $-1$ (with multiplicity $n-1$), so $s^-(K_n)=n-1$. No counterexample was found among graphs on at most 9 vertices.

title: Conjecture 9.3
statement_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ such that $s^{+}(G)=n$. Then $G$ is a bipartite unicyclic graph.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. The authors conjecture that $s^+(G)\ge n$ for every connected graph with $m\ge n+1$, and believe that equality never holds there, i.e. that $s^+(G)=n$ can only occur when $m\le n$. Bipartite unicyclic graphs (connected, with exactly one cycle, of even length) have symmetric spectrum, so $s^+=s^-=m=n$ for them; e.g. $s^+(C_n)=n$ for even $n$. No counterexample was found among graphs on at most 9 vertices.

title: Conjecture 9.4
statement_text: For any connected graph $G$ of order $n$ and $\omega(G)\geq 3$, we have $s^{+}(G)\geq n$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. If the clique number $\omega(G)$ is large one expects $s^+(G)$ to be large, which suggests this refinement of the Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture. It would follow from the authors' conjectures that $s^+(G)\ge n$ whenever $m\ge n+1$ and that unicyclic graphs whose cycle has length $3\pmod4$ satisfy $s^+(G)>n$ (a connected graph with a triangle either has $m\ge n+1$ or is unicyclic with a triangle). The bottleneck is unicyclic graphs with a triangle: the authors' proof for claw-free unicyclic graphs (a triangle with three pendant paths) was already quite a challenge. No counterexample was found among graphs on at most 9 vertices.

title: Conjecture 9.5
statement_text: The following hold: Let $G$ be a maximal planar graph of order $n\geq 10$. Then $s^{+}(G)\geq 3n$. Let $G$ be a maximal outerplanar graph of order $n\geq 8$. Then $s^{+}(G)\geq 2n$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; $n$ is the order and $m$ the size (number of edges). The eigenvalues of $G$ are those of its adjacency matrix, $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$. The positive square energy $s^+(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues, and the negative square energy $s^-(G)$ is the sum of the squares of the negative eigenvalues (so $s^+(G)+s^-(G)=2m$). Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that $\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}\ge n-1$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n$; this is known for regular graphs, hyper-energetic graphs (hence almost all graphs), and with weaker bounds $n-\gamma(G)$ ($\gamma$ the domination number) and $3n/4$ in general. A maximal planar graph is a planar graph to which no edge can be added while preserving planarity (a triangulation), and a maximal outerplanar graph is defined similarly with outerplanarity (all vertices on the outer face). Elphick and Linz noted that the Elphick–Farber–Goldberg–Wocjan conjecture holds for maximal planar graphs and asked whether $s^+(G)\ge3(n-2)$ and $s^-(G)\le3(n-2)$ for connected maximal planar graphs with $n\ge3$. Based on computations and super-additivity, the authors propose this as possibly more accessible. The coefficients cannot be improved: the maximal planar graph $C_{n-2}\vee\overline{K_2}$ (join of a cycle with two non-adjacent vertices) has $s^+=3n+O(\sqrt n)$, and the maximal outerplanar fan $K_1\vee P_{n-1}$ has $s^+\le2n+O(\sqrt n)$.
paper_title: Refinement of a conjecture on positive square energy of graphs
